skill.name: amazon-best-selling-products-finder-api-skill
skill.description: Extract Amazon product research data through a BrowserAct workflow. The skill starts a BrowserAct task from keywords, result limits, and marketplace URLs, then polls task status.
skill.summary: Runs a BrowserAct Amazon product research workflow and reports task progress.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill performs intended outbound calls to BrowserAct and reads BROWSERACT_API_KEY for authentication. Most high secret-key detections are false positives because no hardcoded credential is present, but the docs and script encourage users to provide an API key to the agent. The documentation also markets CAPTCHA and geofencing avoidance for Amazon data extraction, which raises abuse and compliance concerns.

remediation.issue: Credential handling guidance asks users to provide BROWSERACT_API_KEY to the agent.
remediation.suggestion: Change SKILL.md and script messages to instruct users to set BROWSERACT_API_KEY locally. Do not ask users to paste API keys into chat.

remediation.issue: The skill sends authenticated workflow requests and search inputs to BrowserAct.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the external data transfer clearly and ask users to confirm before sending sensitive search terms or marketplace targets.

remediation.issue: The documentation advertises CAPTCHA and geofencing avoidance.
remediation.suggestion: Remove avoidance claims and add guidance to follow Amazon, BrowserAct, rate limit, and regional access requirements.

remediation.issue: The current script appears to return after polling before retrieving task results.
remediation.suggestion: Move timeout handling into a loop else branch or track success so finished tasks continue to the result retrieval request.

content.value_statement: Amazon product research needs current listing data from selected marketplaces. This skill uses BrowserAct to collect product details such as titles, prices, ratings, availability, and product links.
actual_capabilities: Starts a BrowserAct workflow template for Amazon product keyword searches.
Accepts search keywords, a result limit, and an Amazon marketplace URL.
Reads BROWSERACT_API_KEY from the local environment for BrowserAct authentication.
Polls BrowserAct task status and prints timestamped progress updates.
Documents expected fields including title, price, rating, reviews, ASIN, availability, and product URL.
limitations: Requires a BrowserAct API key and sends workflow requests to BrowserAct.
The current script appears to return after polling before retrieving task results.
Product data depends on BrowserAct workflow availability and Amazon marketplace behavior.
Users must verify that automated collection complies with applicable service terms.

use_cases.title: Scan Market Demand
use_cases.description: Collect product listings, ratings, and sales signals for a keyword before sizing a market.

use_cases.title: Compare Competitor Products
use_cases.description: Review prices, promotions, reviews, and availability for products competing with a planned listing.

use_cases.title: Check Regional Availability
use_cases.description: Run the same keyword against different Amazon marketplaces to compare product presence and pricing.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Product Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to search Amazon.com for wireless earbuds with a limit of 10. Show the task status and any returned product summary.

prompt_templates.title: Regional Marketplace Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare one keyword in another region
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Amazon UK for running shoes with a limit of 15. Summarize product names, prices, ratings, reviews, and availability.

prompt_templates.title: Competitor Pricing Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Find best-selling gaming mouse products on Amazon.com. Highlight price ranges, review strength, promotions, and visible sales signals.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-Market Trend Research
prompt_templates.prompt: Run separate searches for portable monitors on Amazon.com and Amazon.de. Compare availability, price patterns, ratings, and product badges.

output_examples.input: Search Amazon.com for wireless earbuds with a limit of 10.
output_examples.output: A concise product research summary with names, current prices, ratings, review counts, availability, and product links when returned.

output_examples.input: Compare running shoes on Amazon UK and Amazon Germany.
output_examples.output: A regional comparison that calls out pricing differences, listing strength, availability, promotions, and notable product badges.

output_examples.input: Find competitor products for a new gaming mouse listing.
output_examples.output: A competitor brief covering common price bands, review volume, rating quality, promotional offers, and visible demand signals.

best_practices: Set BROWSERACT_API_KEY in the local environment before running the script.
Start with a small result limit to confirm the workflow and output quality.
Validate important product data against source listings before business decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into chat or shared logs.
Do not run large repeated searches without checking rate limits and terms.
Do not treat ratings, prices, or sales signals as guaranteed real-time data.

faq.question: Does this skill need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires a BrowserAct API key stored as BROWSERACT_API_KEY in the local environment.

faq.question: Does it scrape Amazon directly from my machine?
faq.answer: No. The script sends workflow requests to BrowserAct, which performs the configured browser workflow.

faq.question: Can I choose an Amazon marketplace?
faq.answer: Yes. The script accepts a marketplace URL such as Amazon.com, Amazon UK, or Amazon Germany.

faq.question: What product fields are expected?
faq.answer: The skill describes titles, brands, prices, ratings, reviews, sales signals, availability, ASINs, badges, and product links.

faq.question: Are returned prices and ratings always current?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on BrowserAct, Amazon availability, and when the workflow runs.

faq.question: Is there a known script issue?
faq.answer: Yes. The current polling flow appears to return before the result retrieval code can run.
